ideas.title: The motor reels in a raft with Truffle aboard
ideas.critique: This is a real step past the motor that barely turned: the motor now has a load it feels, through a rope that goes slack and taut and a hull that floats. Whether it lands depends on Truffle and the rope actually being simulated. If Truffle just sits glued to a raft that gets winched, it is one more device left to run while a fixed camera watches.

ideas.title: The friends pull my first cart up the dune
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This breaks the run of things moving alone: the creatures are the engine, and friction at their feet limits how hard they can pull. It also builds the frame, wheels and rolling contact the cart needs, so it is the strongest step on the road. The danger is a pulling animation that slides along the ground without feet planting, which would undo the whole point.

ideas.title: A roundabout for the friends, turned by the motor
ideas.critique: Riders flung off at the friction limit is something you can watch and want to see again, and the friends love it on screen. But as pitched, each rider is a point mass under one friction inequality on one disc, which is a one-case rig. The belt and the rotating inertia only brush the cart.

ideas.title: The potter's wheel turned by the motor, and turned back by hand
ideas.critique: Running the same machine backwards is a real discovery for the player, and it is a road step the cart's braking needs. Its payoff, though, is a thin wire glowing red and snapping, which is what the last post was. The second half adds little unless the pumping and the drag the player feels against it are what the film shows.

ideas.title: A beach cart race: my motor against Pickles' motor
ideas.critique: A race won by the build and not by reflexes is a goal the player comes back to, and it is the first time a motor moves itself over sand. It needs a drivetrain, traction and a game loop all at once, and it is likely to arrive as two boxes sliding down a strip. A first step that does not visibly race shows nothing.

ideas.title: Sea-water cells in clam shells the friends fill
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: Voltage sagging under load and recovering at rest is a real piece of the cart, and the friends carrying water gives it life. To watch, though, it is a row of props and a motor turning faster, and the friends' fetching risks being a scripted delivery parade.

ideas.title: A motor that sparks in the dark
ideas.critique: Arcs that come from inductance and light the wood and copper are the kind of light a path tracer can show and a game engine cannot. Still, it is the same bench at the same fixed close view, and tuning a spring is a technique more than a goal. It is the most beautiful version of a post the island already has.

ideas.title: Weigh the friends on a seesaw
ideas.critique: Giving creatures a mass from their mesh volume is useful plumbing. A seesaw with a sliding pivot, though, is a known prop with a lever law, and the tipping reactions will most likely be canned.

ideas.title: Copper from green rock
ideas.critique: Making the motor's metal on the island is on the road, and slag when the heat is too low is a fair failure. But a rock that changes colour above a temperature threshold is most likely a phase table written in for one ore. The film is a close fixed view of a material glowing, the same as the glass posts.

ideas.title: A winch that lifts the cairn stones
ideas.critique: It shares the spool-and-rope recipe with the raft idea and adds a first gear. The payoff, though, is a stone rising and being stacked, and the friend who steadies it is probably animation laid on top. Stalling and gearing down is a real choice for the player, but the picture is predictable.
